comment: Profile ids follow <model>-<quant>-<gpus>. A profile lists exactly the platforms it is validated on; resolve() refuses anywhere else. Quant tags: xxs=IQ2_XXS(-Q2_K), q4ktail=Q4K-tail, mxfp4=MXFP4, q4k=Q4_K, q2k=Q2_K.

glm52-vision.title: GLM-5.2-Vision
glm52-vision.shared_note: The mmproj is found by globbing the text GGUF's directory and its parent, so it must sit at the repo root while the shards live in antirez-routed/.

IQ2_XXS.title: UD-IQ2_XXS_RoutedIQ2XXS_blk78Q2K
IQ2_XXS.summary: Maximum throughput and longest context. Noticeably weaker at reasoning and precise transcription; fine for classification, routing, short summarization.

Q2_K.title: UD-Q2_K_RoutedQ2K
Q2_K.summary: The tuned path, and what the published throughput numbers were measured on. Best quality that still fits two MI300X with a large KV pool.

Q4_K.title: UD-Q4_K_RoutedQ4K
Q4_K.summary: Reach for this when the task is precision-sensitive: multi-step tool use, code, math, or reading small text out of images. Quantization error compounds across reasoning steps in a way it does not in summarization.

speculator.note: DSpark draft. Speculation costs quality nothing -- the verifier accepts or rejects every draft token -- so it is on by default.

dsv4-flash.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
dsv4-flash.shared_note: Text only -- this model has no vision tower, so there is no projector to fetch.

speculator.note: Pinned DSpark/DFlash drafter built for the 0731 verifier. Its published DSpark block size is 5, and its draft KV uses TurboQuant.

MXFP4.title: MXFP4Experts (0731)
MXFP4.summary: The tuned path. Routed experts in OCP MXFP4, served through the native GGUF quantized kernels, and the smaller of the two four-GPU builds.

Q4_K.title: Q4KExperts (0731)
Q4_K.summary: Highest quality of the four, imatrix. Every non-expert tensor is identical to the MXFP4 build; only the routed experts differ.

Q4K-tail.title: Layers37-42Q4KExperts (0731)
Q4K-tail.summary: Q4_K on the last six expert layers, IQ2_XXS gate/up with Q2_K down on the rest. Fits two GPUs while keeping the layers nearest the output at higher precision.

IQ2_XXS.title: IQ2XXS-w2Q2K (0731)
IQ2_XXS.summary: Smallest. IQ2_XXS gate/up experts with Q2_K down. On Metal, measured grouped vector MoE is faster than the padded per-expert tile alternative; ROCm and Ampere use native grouped tile paths (A100 pairs gate/up, SwiGLU, and Q8_1 emission before native Q2_K down).

kimi-k3.title: Kimi K3
kimi-k3.shared_note: The vision projector is not in antirez's text repo; it comes from unsloth/Kimi-K3-GGUF. BF16 is preferred because the source vision weights are BF16.

speculator.note: The exact 64-head draft is tensor-sharded at TP8. At TP6 its five-layer backbone is replicated per rank because neither 64 attention heads nor its width divide by six; vocabulary logits remain distributed.

IQ2_XXS-Q2_K.title: Kimi-K3-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K
IQ2_XXS-Q2_K.summary: The only published quant: IQ2_XXS gate/up experts with Q2_K down. 896 routed experts, 93 layers, 24 MLA + 69 KDA.

patch.why: The published file sets kimi-k3.vision = false, which is wrong: the model has a vision tower and the loader skips it otherwise.

assembly.note: Concatenate in lexical order, then apply the patch. Needs 799 GiB free on top of the parts unless the parts are removed as it goes.

muse-glimmer.title: Muse-Glimmer-30B
muse-glimmer.shared_note: The mmproj vision tower is discovered by globbing mmproj* next to the text GGUF, so both live in the repo root of the local dir.

kquant-dynamic.title: K-quant dynamic (per-layer mixed)
kquant-dynamic.summary: The larger of the two published k-quant builds; per-layer mixed precision. Default.

kquant-17gb.title: K-quant 17GB (uniform Q4_K_M)
kquant-17gb.summary: Smaller uniform build for tighter memory; same tokenizer and mmproj.

speculator.note: Published DFlash drafter: 5 layers reading target layers [2, 14, 26, 38, 50], block size 16 (one non-autoregressive block per call). Draft KV uses the default fp16 cache; a TurboQuant draft cache is future work.

NVFP4.title: NVFP4 (mixed FP8+NVFP4)
NVFP4.summary: Unsloth Dynamic v3.0 compressed-tensors checkpoint: NVFP4 g16 on mlp layers 0-55, FP8 E4M3 per-channel on attention, GDN projections, lm_head and mlp 56-63; bf16 embeddings, vision tower and GDN internals. Served as W4A16/W8A16 on Metal.

speculator.note: 2B bf16 DFlash2 drafter (5 non-causal SWA layers + grouped dynamic conv + candidate selector, block_size 8 -> 7 draft tokens). Ships no embed/lm_head: ties to the target's embeddings and fp8-channel lm_head. The trained conv block_size is 8 (1+7 draft tokens); we serve num_speculative_tokens=3 because the measured acceptance horizon on prose is ~3 (UPDATE 27 k-sweep: k=3 beats k=7 by +23% c1). NOT fetch-managed: this is a multi-file directory checkpoint, so slimserve resolves it from ~/models/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 or the HF cache rather than the single-file fetch machinery; `revision` records the gated snapshot but is not enforced by the loader -- pin it manually via huggingface-cli download --revision when installing.

metal.title: Apple Silicon (Metal)
metal.why_gate_is_memory: A Mac is one device with one pool, so counting GPUs says nothing about whether a model fits. Weights, KV and activations all come out of unified memory, and the ceiling that matters is what Metal will let the GPU hold, not what the box advertises.
notes: Metal caps a single MTLBuffer well below total memory -- 80.6 GiB of 128 GiB on an M5 Max. The GGUF loader avoids a file-sized buffer by materializing tensors as separate MPS allocations.
recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize is roughly 90% of physical (115.4 of 128 GiB measured on an M5 Max). The min_memory_bytes figures are physical RAM, chosen to leave that margin plus a KV pool.
No multi-device story: Apple exposes one GPU per machine, so every Metal profile is tensor_parallel_size 1 and scaling past one box means separate machines.

glm52-xxs-1.title: GLM-5.2-Vision on one Mac
glm52-xxs-1.status_reason: GLM-shaped sparse MLA has not been validated on Metal
glm52-xxs-1.status_detail: DeepSeek-V4 now has a measured Metal path, but the separate GLM-shaped sparse-MLA and vision path remains unvalidated. The CLI keeps this profile gated until that model is exercised end to end.
glm52-xxs-1.summary: Single Apple Silicon machine, sized by unified memory rather than card count. Needs 256 GB for IQ2_XXS and 512 GB for Q2_K or Q4_K.
notes: Not yet runnable: this model serves through sparse MLA, and the Metal sparse-MLA kernels do not exist yet. These engine settings are starting points chosen to fit the memory budget, not measured configurations -- unlike every other profile in this file.
Metal has no CUDA-graph equivalent, so graph capture is disabled through compilation_config.

max_num_seqs is deliberately small. Batched serving is the weakest part of every Metal engine surveyed -- ds4 still runs attention and routed experts per session -- so concurrency here is a guess, not a tested ceiling.
DSpark is enabled, with TurboQuant attention and a turboquant_k8v4 draft KV cache.
Q2_K and Q4_K need a 512 GB Mac Studio. IQ2_XXS is the only quant a 256 GB machine can hold.

k3-xxs-6.title: Kimi K3 on 6 GPUs
k3-xxs-6.summary: Tensor parallel across six cards; TP4 does not fit. Two GPUs stay free, and this remains the measured low-concurrency reference while k3-xxs-8 has the highest measured throughput at concurrency 8.
notes: The Kimi verifier keeps its native hybrid cache at auto. The replicated DSpark backbone uses a separate TurboQuant compressed cache on every rank.

The exact draft's 64 query heads, 16 KV heads and 14336 intermediate width do not divide by six. SlimServe therefore replicates the five-layer draft backbone and its small quantized Markov head on each rank; target weights and base vocabulary logits remain distributed.

Target CUDA graphs are disabled for speculative KDA decode: full-decode graphs are not supported for this stateful path, and ROCm piecewise capture can terminate a worker during startup. The DSpark draft graphs are disabled separately.
HSA_XNACK=1 is required for this load.

reasoning_parser must be kimi_k3. K3 frames every channel in XTML rather than with <think>, and the generation prompt opens the first channel, so the parser has to start inside it and drop the closing frame. Under any other parser the answer arrives with "<|close|> response <|sep|> <|close|> message <|sep|>" attached, or -- in thinking mode -- lands entirely in reasoning.

k3-xxs-8.title: Kimi K3 on 8 GPUs
k3-xxs-8.summary: All eight cards on every request: attention tensor-parallel at 12 heads per rank, experts held whole and split 112-per-rank. Expert parallelism is required -- tensor-sharding the experts slices GGUF quant blocks at TP8.
notes: kv_cache_dtype must be 'auto': this fork defaults the cache to fp8 for GLM. fp8 loads and answers correctly here but is a net loss, because K3 is a hybrid. Attention pages must be at least as large as the fixed KDA state page, so halving the per-token attention KV doubles the attention block size (960 -> 1920 tokens) to reach the same page size, and every sequence rounds up to that. Measured on TP6: 344,746 cache tokens and 42.1x concurrency at auto, versus 205,824 and 25.1x at fp8_e4m3.
HSA_XNACK=1 is required for this load.

Target CUDA graphs are disabled for speculative KDA decode: full-decode graphs are not supported for this stateful path, and ROCm piecewise capture can terminate a worker during startup. The DSpark draft graphs are disabled separately.

reasoning_parser must be kimi_k3. K3 frames every channel in XTML rather than with <think>, and the generation prompt opens the first channel, so the parser has to start inside it and drop the closing frame. Under any other parser the answer arrives with "<|close|> response <|sep|> <|close|> message <|sep|>" attached, or -- in thinking mode -- lands entirely in reasoning.

dsv4-xxs-1.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash IQ2_XXS on 1 GPU / Apple Silicon
dsv4-xxs-1.summary: Text only. The smallest 0731 target and its matching DSpark drafter run on one MI300X or a 128 GiB Apple Silicon machine.
notes: block_size must be 256: the DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA backend rejects GLM's 64 with 'no common block size'.
sparse_mla_force_mqa is required, or short prompts take a dense forward the ROCm sparse backend does not implement.
Context comes from the GGUF (1M, yarn over a 65536 base); KV is sized by the default utilization rather than a measured byte budget.
reasoning_parser must be set: this fork defaults it to glm45 for its GLM target, and that parser classifies a whole DeepSeek reply as reasoning, leaving content null for every API client.
Measured on an Apple M5 Max with the IQ2_XXS target, the matching 0731 DSpark drafter, and a TurboQuant k8v4 draft cache.
block_size must be 256 so the target compressor, sparse MLA, and draft cache share compatible pages.
reasoning_parser must be set, or the GLM default classifies a whole DeepSeek reply as reasoning and leaves content null.

The fixed 16 GiB hybrid KV pool is sized to hold one full 262,144-token request (target fp8_ds_mla across 43 layers plus the 3-layer TurboQuant draft cache, ~9 GiB) with margin for concurrent shorter sessions. Weights (80.8 GiB target + 6.5 GiB drafter) plus this pool total ~103 GiB, inside the ~115 GiB Metal working set of a 128 GiB machine. Higher API concurrency drains in scheduler waves instead of paging model weights.
max_model_len is 262144 for real (agentic) use. The 1k-in/2k-out benchmark matrix in perf/baseline_status.md is re-gated under this sizing (see the M1 Ultra campaign entries).

max_num_batched_tokens is 2176 = 2048 + 32 seqs x 4 speculative slots: the scheduler reserves draft-token room, so 2048 would cap scheduled prefill tokens at 1920 and split a 2048-token prompt into two chunks (measured ~230 ms scheduler boundary plus an inefficient 128-token tail chunk).

Long-context status (2026-08-14): the sparse-MLA indexer chain (fused indexer Q rope/quant, prefill top-k, scoring) now has a native Metal implementation, and multi-chunk prefill plus the DSpark verify path are validated at the benchmark matrix on an M1 Ultra. A boot must serve one short decode request before its first multi-chunk prefill (boot-ramp; see vllm/platforms/metal_compat.py). Full 262,144-token serving still needs a dedicated long-context validation pass.

muse-kdyn-1.title: Muse-Glimmer-30B on one Mac
muse-kdyn-1.summary: Vision-language 28B dense model on a single Apple Silicon machine, sized by unified memory. Full 131072-token context; both published k-quants fit a 64 GB Mac.
notes: Interleaved attention: 3 sliding-window (2048) layers per 1 global layer across 52 layers, GQA 32/2, final logit softcapping 20. The hybrid KV manager caps SWA layers at the window, so the 12 GiB pool covers multiple full-context requests on the 13 global layers.
Vision: 50-block CLIP tower at 896 px, patch 14, 2x2 spatial merge into 6656-dim tokens, loaded from the published mmproj GGUF.
DFlash speculation is on by default: the drafter proposes one 16-token block per call against target layers [2, 14, 26, 38, 50].

reasoning_parser must be muse_glimmer: replies use '<|start|>assistant to=self<|message|>...' self-segments, and the fork's glm45 default would classify the whole reply as reasoning, leaving content null.
kv_cache_dtype must be auto (bf16): this fork defaults the KV cache to fp8_e4m3, and the Metal dense/GQA backend has no fp8 KV path.

Performance note (2026-08-11): after the mixed-shard weight-copy fix, no-spec decode measures 12.8 tok/s and DFlash speculation 9.8 tok/s (k=16; k=5 is worse at 7.3 despite equal acceptance). Speculation is net-negative until the small-M GGUF matmul path is fixed -- use --no-spec for best single-stream throughput today. llama.cpp reference on this box: 26.6/50.2.

qwen38-nvfp4-1.title: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 on one Mac
qwen38-nvfp4-1.summary: The NVFP4 quant of record (Unsloth Dynamic v3.0, ~98% of bf16 quality) served as W4A16/W8A16 on a single Apple Silicon machine, with the DFlash2 drafter in batch-adaptive mode: k=3 drafting at batch 1 (+23% c1), drafting off at batch >= 2 (c4/c8 within ~3% of no-spec). Engine settings carried over from the retired qwen38-1 Q4_K_M profile (same architecture and GDN state contracts).
notes: VLLM_QC_MUSE=1 (UPDATE 53, 2026-08-24): the Muse single-command-buffer decode step serves eligible uniform spec-decode batches (m <= 8); everything else falls back to the eager layer loop bit-exactly. c1 17.10 tok/s sha 467b35c3, sha-identical to the pre-muse canonical pin (+4.1%); 2500x64 re-pins to aa448847 (deterministic, TPS flat, 30k needle exact). VLLM_QC_MUSE=0 is the kill switch back to UPDATE 49 behavior. This profile only -- the -tq and -df2 profiles keep muse off (-tq: TQ KV layout untested under the muse attention emit; -df2: preserved as the pre-muse historical gate config).

Speculation is batch-adaptive (source speculator num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size): DFlash2 drafts k=3 only when a single request is running; at batch >= 2 the scheduler sets zero draft slots and the V2 runner skips the drafter forward entirely. Promoted after the 2026-08-21 adaptive gate: c1 13.5-13.6 tok/s sha 8c58a4c6 (bit-exact vs the pinned k=3 twin), c4 ~20.0 / c8 ~23.2 (within ~3% of no-spec).

kv_cache_dtype is explicitly bfloat16, not auto: this checkpoint ships a compressed-tensors kv_cache_scheme (fp8 static), and the fork resolves auto to fp8 when a scheme exists -- but the Metal dense/GQA attention backend has no fp8 KV path. The checkpoint's k/v scales stay available for the later TurboQuant/fp8-KV milestone.

Checkpoint (N0 discovery, HANDOFF.md): compressed-tensors mixed-precision -- NVFP4 g16 (weight_packed U8 [N,K/2] + weight_scale F8_E4M3 [N,K/16] + weight_global_scale F32) on mlp layers 0-55; FP8 E4M3 per-channel (weight F8 [N,K] + weight_scale BF16 [N,1]) on attn qkvo, GDN qkv/z/out, lm_head, mlp 56-63. Input-activation quant in the checkpoint is ignored on Metal: both schemes serve as weight-only (W4A16/W8A16) against bf16 activations.
model_mtp.safetensors is the model's own MTP head (bf16, mtp.* names in the weight-map index) -- excluded from the base-model load; speculation via qwen3_5_mtp is a later milestone.

Engine settings inherited from the retired qwen38-1 Q4_K_M profile (same architecture, same GDN state contracts): V2 runner forced, DS conv layout, fp32 mamba cache, prefix caching off for hybrid state.
eos per this checkpoint's config.json is 248044 (the GGUF campaign used 248046); verify against the served tokenizer during bring-up.

qwen38-nvfp4-1-tq.title: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 + TurboQuant KV (experimental)
qwen38-nvfp4-1-tq.summary: N6 experiment: identical to qwen38-nvfp4-1 except the 16 full-attention layers and the DFlash2 drafter run the TurboQuant backend with a turboquant_k8v4 KV cache (tq_attention_combined hs256/hs128 Metal kernels). GDN state pages are unchanged. Not the serving default until quality- and throughput-gated.
notes: TurboQuant applies to the target's 16 full-attention layers AND the DFlash2 drafter's 5 layers (DSV4 DSpark drafter precedent); the 48 GDN layers keep their fp32/DS state pages via mamba_cache_dtype.

Both drafter fields must be pinned together. Unset, the drafter inherits the engine-global turboquant_k8v4 dtype but keeps the metal_attn backend, and the TQ-sized page cannot be viewed with metal_attn's 5-dim cache shape (boot reshape failure). A bf16 drafter dtype fails earlier: its 4096-byte/token page cannot pad to the TQ-aligned max page because metal_attn does not index KV by block stride (unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size NotImplementedError). Drafter-on-TQ makes both quanta 1728 bytes/token (4x432 target hs256, 8x216 drafter hs128) and TQ pads by block stride.

GATED 2026-08-21 (UPDATE 36, re-gated through UPDATE 46 on the full U43/U44/U45 stack): needle recall exact at 4.5k multi-chunk prefill and at the 262k config, deterministic 2/2 per leg. Pins: c1 228d0bf4 (bit-exact through UPDATE 46); 2500x64 d0e07ddd — still the CANONICAL sha; tail 2100x32 1337d2f7. TPS (UPDATE 46, all legs re-measured): c1 16.18-16.24 (-1.2% vs canonical 16.43); 2500x64 3.51 (+1.4% above canonical); c4 23.62-23.72 (+2.4%); c8 26.05-26.09 (+1.8%). -tq beats canonical on every leg above c1 with 2.4x KV capacity; default flip remains a flagged quality decision (k8v4 cos ~0.9955 floor).

Decode attention (UPDATE 40): tq_attention_splitk + tq_attention_reduce (PA256-style split-K, one simdgroup per token, block-table direct) on the hs256 route; VLLM_QC_TQ_SPLITK=0 restores the monolithic kernel. Kernel 12-33x over monolithic; TQ decode reads 432 B/token vs bf16's 1024 and is ~2x faster than canonical PA256 at 32k context.

Continuation prefill (>128-token chunks) runs dequant-once via tq_decode_combined + SDPA (KV-tiled fp32 online softmax past 8k context); small chunks keep the synthetic-decode kernel. The pre-UPDATE-39 synthetic-decode-for-everything route made long prefill O(ctx^2) with a ~24x-redundant constant (16k prefill 406 s vs 111 s now).

LONG-CONTEXT VALIDATED 2026-08-21 (UPDATE 39): with --ctx 262144 (native max_position_embeddings, no rope scaling) the needle ladder passes EXACT at 16k/65k/131k/262k depths; the 262k leg = 259,888 prompt tokens, 75 min prefill. Prefill cost model T(C) ~= 6.4e-3*C + 3.9e-8*C^2 seconds. Canonical bf16 cannot admit a 262k request; this profile holds 292,882 KV tokens.

Use case: capacity/long-context — k8v4 compresses full-attn KV 4096 -> 1728 bytes/token (~2.4x, target and drafter). Measured: 292,882 KV tokens vs canonical 158,038 under the same 16 GiB budget (1.85x; 8.94x vs 4.82x concurrency at 32k). Since UPDATE 40 this profile also wins on throughput at c4/c8/2500x64 and trails c1 by 0.8%; the canonical default is a flagged quality decision (k8v4 KV cos ~0.9955 floor vs bf16), not a TPS one.
Engine settings otherwise identical to qwen38-nvfp4-1 (adaptive DFlash2 spec, V2 runner, DS conv layout, async scheduling).
